description: Solo team from Indonesia building Left Behind, an interactive storytelling map of NASA hardware left on the Moon and Mars.
summary: Left Behind is an interactive storytelling map of 23 sites where NASA hardware rests on the Moon and Mars, from Ranger 7 (1964) to the Ingenuity helicopter (2021). Students pick a world, click a site and discover what was left there: descent stages, rovers, rocket stages, crash sites, plaques, a family photo, a DVD library and a sample depot. Each site shows its year, approximate mass and location, a short human story, and the science it made possible. For example, the LCROSS crash confirmed water ice at the lunar south pole, which is why Artemis is going there. Colour coding separates crewed, robotic and impact sites, and a tonnage counter shows how much we have left behind. The project addresses the challenge by turning 'discarded equipment' into a museum of exploration that introduces school-age space fans to the hardware and its science. It is a lightweight static web app with no API keys and no tracking, and it works on phones and low-end devices, so classrooms anywhere can use it.
details: What it does: Left Behind maps 23 sites where NASA hardware rests on the Moon (12) and Mars (11). A Moon/Mars toggle redraws an equirectangular SVG map. Each dot is sized by approximate mass and coloured by type (crewed, robotic, impact/crash). Clicking a dot or list card opens a story card: what was left, year, mass, coordinates, a human story, and the science legacy. Benefits: it turns abstract 'space junk' into memorable stories for school-age learners (Charlie Duke's family photo, the Fallen Astronaut memorial, LCROSS finding water ice, Ingenuity carrying a piece of the Wright Flyer) and links each object to the science it enabled. Tools: plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with inline SVG; no frameworks, no API keys, no tracking; hosted as static files on nginx. Creativity and design factors: a museum-label storytelling format, accessibility on low-end phones and slow networks for classrooms in Indonesia and elsewhere, and respectful framing of memorial sites. Coordinates are approximate and taken from public NASA mission records. Next steps: LRO/HiRISE photos for each site, deep-space hardware (Voyager, Pioneer, New Horizons), a Bahasa Indonesia translation and a teacher quiz mode.
